frequency_question: How often do partisan electoral reform bills pass the U.S. Senate within a 1-year window from introduction or major advancement?
membership_rule: Bills specifically targeting federal voting requirements (e.g., voter ID, registration rules) considered in the U.S. Senate between 2000 and 2025; excludes routine appropriations or bipartisan postal voting adjustments.
coverage_note: 4 named major federal electoral reform pushes in the Senate over two decades; HAVA was notably bipartisan, while subsequent strict partisan bills failed due to the filibuster.
known_gaps: Minor technical amendments to election laws are excluded as they do not match the profile of high-profile voter eligibility mandates.
validity_reason: The baseline structural hurdle (the 60-vote filibuster threshold for legislation in the Senate) remains stable through this period.
